Recorded at importance 0 so this accident is not re-examined; it is the fifth substring collision in the index and the first caused by a typo.

repo-aiprogrammer.summary: A Chinese-language magazine on AI programming, published as dated article directories. One issue covers SDV across two articles, one using the older top-level `SDV` class and another the current `CTGANSynthesizer` with `SingleTableMetadata`. The entry records SDV reaching a non-English practitioner audience.

repo-wayland.summary: An agent platform organized around a library of skill definitions the agent loads at run time. Its synthetic-data skill packages SDV as a capability the agent can invoke, with `Metadata`, `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer` and `CTGANSynthesizer` in a runnable example. SDV is executed on demand rather than declared as a dependency of the platform.

paper-reproducible-synthetic-socio-digit.summary: This paper presents a reproducible, openly released synthetic dataset of socio-digital support networks reconstructed from aggregate field statistics collected in three rural community-based tourism communities in Guayas, Ecuador, aimed at studying digital inequality via social network analysis. The repository provides synthetic actor metadata, directed support networks across multiple socio-digital dimensions, and precomputed SNA indicators, distributed in formats compatible with NetworkX, Gephi, Neo4j, and graph-learning tools. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in the reference list as prior work on synthetic data generation, with no SDV component or method actually used or described in the text.

paper-adaptive-gans-domain-specific-2026.summary: This paper proposes a domain-adaptive Conditional GAN framework with specialized, theoretically grounded loss functions and adaptive weight adjustment mechanisms for handling extreme data imbalance in healthcare (Wisconsin Breast Cancer) and finance (Credit Card Fraud) datasets. It reports large gains in feature correlation preservation and F1-score over prior methods across imbalance ratios from 1:10 to 1:2000. CTGAN is cited in related work as an example of dynamic loss weight tuning in GAN settings, informing the authors' own adaptive weighting mechanism, but is not run in the experiments described.
paper-adaptive-gans-domain-specific-2026.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is only cited or whether any empirical comparison against it appears in the full paper.

paper-advancing-cardiovascular-disease-d.summary: This paper develops a machine learning ecosystem for cardiovascular disease diagnosis combining tabular neural networks (TabNet, TabPFN), ensemble methods, SHAP/counterfactual interpretability, fairness auditing, Bayesian uncertainty quantification, and causal inference, validated on multi-regional heart-disease datasets. As part of a multi-stage bias mitigation pipeline, the authors apply SMOTE for class balancing and CTGAN to generate synthetic instances that equalize diseased/healthy frequencies across sexes to reduce demographic bias, reporting improved fairness metrics after retraining. CTGAN's conditional generation and mode-specific normalization mechanism are described and cited to Xu et al. (2019), with CTGAN run as one stage among several in the pipeline rather than as the paper's core contribution.
paper-advancing-cardiovascular-disease-d.needs: Not verifiable from text whether CTGAN was run via the ctgan/sdv-dev package or a custom implementation; treated as api_user given no explicit reimplementation language.

paper-application-gan-augmentation-filte.summary: This paper proposes GAN-based data augmentation combined with filtering methods to address class imbalance in classifying grinding wheel specifications, an industrial manufacturing quality/inspection task. It appears to use CTGAN-style generation to synthesize minority-class samples before filtering and classification. CTGAN, from the SDV family, is cited and apparently used as a generator for the augmentation pipeline.
paper-application-gan-augmentation-filte.needs: Full text needed to confirm whether CTGAN was run via the SDV/ctgan package (api_user) or reimplemented (port), and whether it served as the sole generator or one of several baselines.

paper-assessing-robustness-evaluation-me.summary: This paper investigates whether commonly used fidelity, diversity, privacy, and utility metrics for synthetic biomedical time-series remain reliable indicators of signal quality under controlled perturbations, using synthetic ECGs generated by five models (SSSD-ECG, WaveGAN*, Pulse2Pulse, cNVAE-ECG, and YData's proprietary model). It finds that metric robustness varies by quality dimension, with density and coverage behaving as expected while many other commonly used metrics fail to reflect meaningful degradation. The CTGAN paper is cited among the generative-modeling literature but CTGAN itself is not one of the models evaluated.
paper-assessing-robustness-evaluation-me.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm the context or purpose of the CTGAN citation, or whether any CTGAN-derived component was actually used.

paper-construction-multi-stage-heat-2026.summary: This paper builds a multi-stage heat release prediction model for a high-pressure direct injection diesel/natural gas dual-fuel engine, combining active subspace sensitivity analysis, triple Wiebe function fitting, and support vector regression tuned via GridSearchCV to predict heat release rate from engine operating parameters. To overcome the limited size of the experimental training dataset and improve generalization, the authors use CTGAN to augment the original data before recalibrating the model. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN, is run as the data augmentation generator that expands the engine's limited training set.
paper-construction-multi-stage-heat-2026.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether SDV's CTGAN package was run directly or reimplemented, so api_user is inferred from typical usage pattern rather than confirmed code/library reference.

paper-health-state-diagnosis-power-2026.summary: A conference paper proposing to diagnose power transformer health states using dissolved gas analysis (DGA) data that has been augmented with CTGAN to address limited/imbalanced fault data. The work frames CTGAN as the data-augmentation mechanism underlying its diagnosis pipeline, citing prior demonstrations of its advantages for DGA data augmentation. CTGAN, the SDV-family tabular GAN, is used as the generator to produce the augmented training data on which the diagnosis method is built.
paper-health-state-diagnosis-power-2026.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was run directly, reimplemented, or whether conditional sampling was used to address class imbalance in fault types.

paper-identifying-pertinent-cohorts-addr.summary: This work addresses class imbalance in intensive care unit survival analysis, aiming to identify pertinent patient cohorts and improve robustness of survival prediction models. No further methodological detail is available beyond the metadata and citation list. The paper cites the CTGAN paper from the SDV family, suggesting CTGAN may be used or discussed as a technique for addressing data imbalance, though this cannot be confirmed from the available evidence.
paper-identifying-pertinent-cohorts-addr.needs: Full text and citing sentence not available; cannot determine whether CTGAN was run (api_user), used as inspiration (citation_only), or reimplemented (port). Metadata-only tier limits confidence.

paper-insect-wing-structured-microfluidi.summary: This paper presents a dragonfly-wing-inspired PDMS microfluidic chip used as a physical reservoir for pattern classification, where RGB dye patterns are transformed through fluid channels, imaged by a camera, and classified by a trained readout layer. To address limited real training data, the authors compare two synthetic data augmentation strategies -- Gaussian noise perturbation and a generative model -- evaluating classification accuracy across record counts and quantization settings. CTGAN, explicitly identified as "a model provided by Synthetic Data Vault (SDV)," is trained directly on quantized reservoir outputs to generate synthetic records, run as one of two data-augmentation methods and found to underperform the simpler Gaussian approach.

paper-mt2m-strategic-cost-optimization-2.summary: This paper proposes MT2M, a Bayesian Stackelberg game-theoretic framework for Moving Target Defense that optimizes cybersecurity costs by linearizing an NP-hard resource-allocation problem, achieving comparable security with up to 15% cost reduction in simulations. The CTGAN paper is cited only in passing, alongside another reference, to support the general claim that machine-learning solutions are not guaranteed to be good and require traditional mathematical modeling. CTGAN itself is not run or otherwise engaged with in the visible text.
paper-mt2m-strategic-cost-optimization-2.needs: Full text not available; abstract does not mention CTGAN or synthetic data at all, so it is unclear whether the paper engages with CTGAN beyond a passing citation.

paper-modeling-longitudinal-student-path.summary: This paper proposes a scalable, explainable framework for generating synthetic longitudinal student pathway data using a dynamic Bayesian network trained on multi-table community college records, showing it better reproduces marginal, conditional, and higher-order patterns than an independent sampler while remaining interpretable. It also analyzes k-anonymity's infeasibility for real or synthetic student data. CTGAN is cited only in passing in the related-work survey of generative modeling techniques for tabular data, not run or compared against experimentally.
paper-modeling-longitudinal-student-path.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether CTGAN is used anywhere beyond the related-work mention.

paper-predicting-corporate-management-pe.summary: This study builds an AI-based prediction model for corporate management performance in Korean listed firms by combining financial variables with strategic signals mined from CEO messages in sustainability reports, categorized via the Sustainable Balanced Scorecard framework. Eight classifiers (including KNN, SVM, GBM, CatBoost, GAN, RNN, LSTM, Transformer) are compared under 5-fold cross-validation, with the Transformer plus SBSC features achieving the best performance. CTGAN is cited in the related-work discussion as an example of a conditional GAN variant designed to model mixed-type tabular distributions, motivating the inclusion of a GAN-based classifier, but the paper does not indicate that the SDV CTGAN implementation itself was run.
paper-predicting-corporate-management-pe.needs: Unclear whether the 'GAN' classifier used in experiments is an actual CTGAN implementation or an unrelated GAN-based classifier inspired by the cited design; no library name or hyperparameters are given.

paper-recommendation-how-use-synthetic-2.summary: This paper investigates how mixing real and synthetic tabular data in different proportions affects downstream ML model performance, using three datasets (MHealth, HEPMass, UCBP) and three classifiers (Decision Tree, Gaussian Naive Bayes, Linear SVM) evaluated via 5-fold cross-validation and paired t-tests. It provides practical recommendations on optimal real-to-synthetic ratios for maximising model accuracy. CTGAN and TVAE are run directly (via a Streamlit dashboard, with modified hyperparameters such as batch size) as the two synthetic data generators underpinning the entire empirical study.
paper-recommendation-how-use-synthetic-2.needs: Not explicit whether the sdv or ctgan pip package (which bundles TVAE) was used, or a separate TVAE implementation; assumed ctgan package given joint CTGAN/TVAE handling and hyperparameter language.

paper-stacking-ensemble-framework-intrus.summary: This conference paper proposes a stacking ensemble framework using tree-based models to detect cyberattacks (e.g., DDoS, SQL injection, false data injection) targeting Internet-of-Energy systems, particularly battery energy storage systems, and evaluates it for detection accuracy and computational efficiency. To address severe class imbalance in the intrusion dataset, the authors generate additional minority-class ('Attack') instances using a tabular variational autoencoder. TVAE, the SDV-family generative model, is run as the data augmentation tool to oversample the minority class in the training pipeline.
paper-stacking-ensemble-framework-intrus.needs: No explicit mention of the sdv-dev/ctgan package or code; unclear whether the authors ran the library's TVAE implementation or an independent one, so api_user vs. port cannot be fully confirmed.

paper-synthetic-tabular-health-generatio.summary: This paper reviews and empirically compares statistical data-simulation approaches (correlation- and model-based) against generative adversarial network approaches for producing synthetic tabular health data, aiming to guide practitioners on which method to use for privacy protection, data sharing, and prediction-model validation. The empirical study evaluates both families on real-world health datasets, assessing how closely synthetic data resembles real data structure and supports downstream prediction performance. CTGAN, the conditional generative adversarial network for tabular data, is run as one of the two main approaches compared throughout the empirical evaluation.
paper-synthetic-tabular-health-generatio.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was used directly (api_user) or a reimplementation (port), nor exact affiliations of authors.

paper-taming-challenges-security-tasks-2.summary: This paper investigates whether Generative AI can address data challenges (class imbalance, sparse samples, concept drift) that limit ML-based security classifiers, evaluating 7 security tasks against 6 state-of-the-art GenAI methods and introducing a new controlled-synthesis scheme called Nimai. Among the baselines compared is TVAE, described and run with its variational Gaussian-mixture mode-specific normalization and rejection sampling for class-conditional generation, alongside CTAB-GAN+, TabDDPM, GReaT, REaLTabFormer and TabSyn. TVAE, the variational-autoencoder synthesizer shipped as part of the CTGAN package, is run as one of several evaluation-subject generators whose data-augmentation performance is measured across the security tasks, not as the paper's own proposed model.
paper-taming-challenges-security-tasks-2.needs: The specific sentence OpenAlex ties to sdv-dsaa-2016 (a list of security-application citations) does not itself mention SDV; the actual SDV-family engagement found in the body is TVAE run as one of several GenAI baselines. It is unclear whether TVAE was invoked via the official ctgan/sdv library or reimplemented, since no import or package name is stated.

paper-advancing-colorectal-cancer-diagno.summary: This book chapter investigates the role of gut microbiota shifts in the progression from advanced adenomatous polyps to colorectal cancer, using synthetic data augmentation to enlarge and balance an OTU (microbiome) table for machine-learning classification, followed by deep-learning feature extraction (LRP, SHAP, XGBoost) to identify discriminative bacterial taxa such as Fusobacterium and Parvimonas across stool, biopsy, and saliva datasets. The synthetic data generation step underlying this augmented OTU table is the point of contact with the SDV family, though the specific component or model used is not identifiable from the available evidence.
paper-advancing-colorectal-cancer-diagno.needs: Full text and citing sentence not obtained; cannot confirm which SDV component (e.g., CTGAN, GaussianCopula) was used for the synthetic OTU data augmentation or how central it was to the empirical pipeline.

paper-bridging-generation-gap-age-2025.summary: This paper proposes FC-TVAE, a Fairness-Constrained Tabular Variational Autoencoder that adds a maximum-mean-discrepancy regularizer to enforce age-band demographic parity when generating synthetic customer profiles from the Kaggle Customer Personality Analysis dataset. The authors benchmark FC-TVAE against a Baseline TVAE, a Conditional GAN, FairGAN, and DP-WGAN on reconstruction MSE, demographic-parity gap, and minority-group recall. The Baseline TVAE and the proposed FC-TVAE are the authors' own reimplementation of the TVAE architecture (custom encoder/decoder MLPs with Gumbel-softmax and Gaussian decoder heads), described in the authors' own prose rather than run via the SDV package, with CTGAN cited only in the related-work discussion of prior tabular generative models.
paper-bridging-generation-gap-age-2025.needs: Confirm whether 'Conditional GAN' baseline refers to CTGAN specifically or a generic conditional GAN; the text never names the SDV library or ctgan package directly, only cites CTGAN/TGAN in a reference list context.

paper-classification-regression-efficien.summary: Compares CTGAN and TVAE across both classification and regression tasks, noting that most published comparisons cover only the former. Both methods under test are SDV's, so the contribution is an account of how the library's two deep synthesizers behave when the target is continuous.

paper-debate-decide-deliberative-multi-2.summary: This paper proposes Debate-to-Decide, a multi-agent LLM framework that reframes student credit scoring as a transparent, argumentation-based deliberation among specialized agents rather than a black-box prediction, benchmarking it against an XGBoost baseline on accuracy, fairness, and explainability. To obtain a rigorous and privacy-preserving evaluation dataset, the authors expand a small expert-labeled seed set of 300 student profiles into 10,000-1,500 synthetic records. CTGAN is run as the sole synthetic-data generator that produces the entire evaluation dataset underpinning the framework's empirical results.
paper-debate-decide-deliberative-multi-2.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV's own ctgan package was invoked or a reimplementation was used, though CTGAN naming and use pattern suggest the standard library.

paper-explicit-analysis-vivo-meterologic.summary: This review examines why nanomedicines with promising preclinical results often fail during clinical translation, covering issues such as pathophysiological complexity, misuse of statistical tools, EPR-effect variability, and manufacturing challenges. It argues for incorporation of simulation models and synthetic data to strengthen preclinical statistical frameworks and proposes CTGAN as an 'innovative tool' that could help bridge the preclinical-clinical divide. CTGAN is only cited in passing as a data-synthesis technique capable of generating statistically realistic records, without being implemented or evaluated in the paper.
paper-explicit-analysis-vivo-meterologic.needs: Only an abstract and one citing sentence were available; full text not obtained, so depth of engagement with CTGAN beyond a passing mention cannot be confirmed.

paper-ganesis-generative-adversarial-net.summary: This conference paper introduces GANesis, a GAN architecture with improved generator/discriminator normalization, Xavier initialization, and adaptive optimization, aimed at generating synthetic tabular demographic data (UCI Adult dataset) that preserves feature correlations and trains stably. It compares its loss-convergence results against other published tabular-synthesis methods (Bt-GAN, CTAB-GAN+, CTGAN-MOS) in a table, but none of these are SDV-family models actually re-run by the authors. TGAN and CTGAN are discussed in the literature review as prior GAN-based tabular synthesis approaches the authors' architecture is positioned against, but neither is executed or benchmarked directly.
paper-ganesis-generative-adversarial-net.needs: No citing sentences or full text available; cannot verify whether CTGAN/TGAN are substantively discussed as prior art or merely listed in the bibliography. Abstract-only tier caps confidence.

paper-generative-adversarial-evasion-out.summary: This paper proposes a conditional GAN (cGAN)-based framework that crafts stealthy adversarial attacks against UAV intrusion detection systems, paired with a conditional variational autoencoder that uses negative log-likelihood to distinguish these adversarial samples from genuine out-of-distribution telemetry data. The cGAN targets UAV cyber-attack types (DoS, false data injection, MiTM, replay) and is compared against Mahalanobis-distance-based OOD detectors. CTGAN's paper is cited only in passing as a reference for how a conditional GAN can be trained in a standard manner, with no use of the SDV library or its methodology.

paper-geochemical-isotopic-studies-douda.summary: This is a hydrogeochemical and isotopic study of the Douda-Damerjogue aquifer in Djibouti, investigating the sources of high nitrate and fluoride concentrations, mapping their spatial distribution, assessing associated human health risks, and applying machine learning to predict water quality. The work is environmental/geochemical in nature with no described synthetic-data generation task. It cites the SDV foundational paper (Patki et al. 2016), but the evidence gives no indication of any SDV component being run or engaged with substantively.

paper-iar-net-catheterization-2025.summary: Recognises catheterization actions from tabular sensor features to give interventionalists objective, immediate feedback in place of subjective assessment. Six generative models are evaluated to expand the training set, and the abstract singles out CTGAN as the exception to otherwise high fidelity scores, which makes this one of the few entries recording a negative result for an SDV synthesizer.

paper-steam-causal-synthetic-2025.summary: Argues that synthetic medical data judged only on marginal fidelity can still mislead a downstream causal analysis, and proposes STEAM, which structures generation around a causal graph so that each variable is generated conditional on its parents, together with evaluation targets aimed at causal rather than distributional faithfulness. CTGAN is both a compared generic generator and a substrate STEAM is applied to: the results tables carry a CTGAN row and a STEAM CTGAN row side by side across the datasets, with the STEAM version reported as improving precision and treatment-effect error.

Recorded api_user 4 here instead, on the reading that STEAM structures generation AROUND a frozen CTGAN rather than entering its losses, which is the GAN_BERT composition test. The two entries should be ruled together, and this is the third model-agnostic-wrapper case after shard 60 and paper-rule-guided-tabular-low-data-2025 in shard 71

paper-latent-diffusion-models-correlatio.summary: This paper proposes a latent diffusion model for tabular data generation that maps data into a latent space via autoencoders, learns the latent distribution through a diffusion process, and adds an explicit correlation loss plus a reconstruction-conditioned diffusion step to better capture attribute correlations. It evaluates the method against TVAE, CTGAN, CTAB-GAN and TabDDPM baselines on the Adult and Covertype datasets using column-shape, column-pair-trend and ML-efficacy metrics. CTGAN and TVAE, both attributed to the cited CTGAN paper, are run only as comparison baselines that the proposed diffusion model is shown to outperform.

paper-learning-manage-investment-portfol.summary: This paper proposes a GAN-based generative framework that models a fund manager's portfolio weight decisions as a conditional distribution over stock characteristics, historical returns, and a latent strategy variable, validated on 1436 U.S. equity mutual funds to recover interpretable investment styles like growth and value. It is not a tabular-data synthesis paper itself but cites CTGAN in passing as prior work adapted for financial tasks including portfolio optimization. CTGAN is only cited bibliographically, never run or engaged with in the body text.

paper-model-interpretability-private-saf.summary: This paper proposes a privacy-preserving pipeline for predicting student dropout that uses a modified Preprocessed Kernel Inducing Points data distillation technique to generate synthetic training samples instead of using real student data, paired with SHAP-based interpretability to justify high-risk classifications for educational management. The authors report their distillation approach outperforms 'traditional data synthesis techniques such as the Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks' in performance and efficiency. CTGAN is cited only as prior art the proposed method is compared against in the abstract's framing; no SDV-family term appears anywhere in the full text outside the bibliography.

paper-pasteur-scaling-privacy-aware-2025.summary: This paper presents Pasteur, a system for scaling privacy-aware data synthesis to larger-than-memory relational datasets on a single server, using parallelization, optimized memory representations, and an accelerated marginal-calculation algorithm for PGM-based synthesis, demonstrating billion-row synthesis in one hour on a 16-core CPU. SDV is mentioned in related work as a data synthesis system (collection of algorithms and evaluation metrics) that, unlike Pasteur, does not attempt scaling or larger-than-memory synthesis, and SDV is otherwise only cited, not run.
paper-pasteur-scaling-privacy-aware-2025.needs: Only metadata was available (no abstract or citing sentences); cannot confirm whether SDV is run, compared, or merely cited in passing. Full text needed to verify integration type and importance.

paper-realistic-synthetic-dataset-genera.summary: This paper evaluates DoppelGANger, a time-series GAN, for generating synthetic cyber-physical-system (CPS) data across four real-world testbeds (water distribution, HAI, gas pipeline, power system), assessing fidelity via silhouette scores, correlation analysis, t-SNE visualizations and anomaly detection. In a computational-efficiency comparison, the authors also train TimeGAN and CTGAN to benchmark implementation time against DoppelGANger, while separately discussing the CPAR sequential model within the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) framework as prior related work. CTGAN is run as one of several baseline generators for timing comparison, while SDV's PAR/CPAR sequential synthesizer is only cited and discussed, not executed.

paper-synthetic-2025.summary: A book chapter on synthetic data, apparently surveying methods and concepts in the field. No abstract or full text was available to determine its specific scope or contribution. It cites the SDV DSAA 2016 paper (the original Synthetic Data Vault paper) as a reference.

paper-synthetic-tabular-generation-vae-2.summary: This paper proposes T-VAE-GAN, a hybrid generative model for tabular synthetic data generation that hierarchically combines GANs and VAEs to jointly achieve high sample quality and accurate modeling of the original data distribution, evaluated across many datasets against leading tabular SDG approaches. The paper cites the CTGAN paper as prior art in the GAN-based tabular synthesis literature its method is positioned against. CTGAN is referenced as a comparison point among the leading GAN/VAE approaches for tabular data generation, though the evidence available does not confirm whether it was actually run as an experimental baseline.

paper-trace-transformer-risk-assessment-.summary: This paper proposes TRACE, a Transformer-based architecture for clinical risk assessment that handles multi-modal (continuous, categorical, checkbox) data and missing values, using self-attention for interpretability and outperforming baselines on clinical datasets including a highly imbalanced BRFSS22 dataset. The authors address class imbalance primarily via focal loss but also benchmark oversampling techniques as baselines. CTGAN is run as one of several baseline oversampling methods (alongside SMOTE and downsampling), with its PAC and hidden-layer hyperparameters reported, to generate synthetic minority-class samples for comparison.

paper-physician-workforce-forecasting-sd.summary: Forecasts physician supply and demand in Turkey to 2030 for the NACE Q sector of human health and social work activities, which the authors put at roughly 5.5 percent of national employment, on the argument that medical training is long and costly so a shortage cannot be corrected in the short term and must be planned for. OECD series covering 1979-2018 for demand and 2000-2019 for supply drive a supply model with medical-school graduates per 100,000 people, emigrating physicians and foreign physicians as regressors, and a demand model with GDP per capita, the out-of-pocket share of health expenditure and the over-65 population share, fitted with XGBoost, random forest, LSTM and Facebook Prophet under walk-forward validation and scored by RMSE. Because annual data leaves too few points for machine learning, the authors generate synthetic replicas with the Synthetic Data Vault and repeat the entire exercise on them, producing 100,000 observations for each of the supply and demand sets and trying 2,000- and 10,000-observation variants to check whether size changes the similarity scores. On real data XGBoost has the lowest error and puts 2030 supply at 3.04 and demand at 3.12 physicians per 1,000 people; on synthetic data LightGBM and gradient boosting give 2.03 and 2.86, agreeing with the real-data result on the direction of the gap, which is the paper's headline finding. The entry records SDV as the source of that synthetic half of the study: the sdv.tabular.GaussianCopula model is named as the generator, the enter-data-and-schemas then fit then sample workflow is described from SDV's own documentation, the PAR model is noted for the time-series case, and SDV's evaluate function supplies both the similarity scores and the metric table in the appendix.

paper-hybrid-machine-learning-designing-.summary: This paper develops a design-optimization method for an XY compliant mechanism that maximizes fatigue life under small-sample-size fatigue data, using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to enlarge the training set, a machine-learning surrogate model to predict fatigue life, and the Hunger Games Search algorithm to optimize the mechanism's dimensions, validated against ANSYS simulations. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing as an alternative data-augmentation method that, unlike the chosen SMOTE approach, requires a large amount of training data to generate new samples well, and is not used in the study.

paper-augmenting-small-biomedical-datase.summary: This paper proposes an unsupervised generative algorithm based on emergent self-organizing maps (ESOMs) that augments small multivariate biomedical datasets by generating new points within adapted hyperspheres around detected data structures, validated on synthetic and omics datasets (transcriptomics, lipidomics). The authors compare their ESOM-based method against several existing generative approaches, including Gaussian mixture models and GAN-based tabular synthesizers. TGAN and CTGAN (linked via sdv.dev and the sdv-dev GitHub repositories) are run as baseline generators whose outputs are shown alongside the proposed method's results in comparative figures, but are found less satisfactory than the ESOM approach.

paper-boosting-fair-classifier-generaliz.summary: This paper proposes an adaptive reweighing method that weights training samples by their distance to the decision boundary, aiming to improve the generalizability of fairness constraints (equal opportunity, equalized odds, demographic parity) across tabular, language and vision benchmarks. Among its five evaluation datasets, one is a synthetic tabular dataset of 70,000 samples with gender as the sensitive attribute for an income-prediction task. CTGAN is run as the generator that produces this synthetic benchmark dataset used to test the fairness method.

paper-clues-collusive-theft-conditional-.summary: This paper presents CLUES, a collusive model-stealing framework in which multiple adversarial 'thieves' collude to query a deployed conditional GAN service and jointly train a stolen generator via federated learning, evaluated on MNIST, FashionMNIST and CelebA against throttling, noise, watermarking and JPEG-based defenses. The work is about image-generating cGAN theft, not tabular synthesis. CTGAN is cited only in passing, as an example of cGANs applied to tabular data alongside CTAB-GAN, with no experiments run on it.

paper-explainable-artificial-intelligenc.summary: This paper develops an explainable AI framework to predict the plastic hinge length of flexural-dominated steel-reinforced concrete composite shear walls, presumably using machine learning models trained on experimental data and interpreted with explainability techniques. No abstract or full text was available to confirm the specifics of the modeling pipeline or dataset construction. The work cites the CTGAN paper, but the evidence gives no indication of whether CTGAN was actually run or merely referenced.

paper-forecasting-population-migration-s.summary: This paper addresses population migration forecasting for small settlements in Russia, where reliable data are scarce, by mining textual municipal reports and using generative models to build synthetic training samples for a downstream classifier-regressor pipeline. The authors trained and compared three tabular generators -- CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN -- evaluating synthetic data quality via Jensen-Shannon divergence, correlation similarity, and a classifier two-sample test, ultimately selecting TVAE for small-city data augmentation feeding the migration forecasting models. SDV's CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN synthesizers (the latter explicitly linked to docs.sdv.dev) are all run as evaluated generators, with the SDV library forming the empirical backbone of the entire synthetic-data pipeline.

paper-gans-panorama-synthetic-generation.summary: This article reviews GAN architectures for tabular synthetic data generation (TGAN, CTGAN, TabFairGAN) and applies them to a fake news detection case study, using synthetic data to augment an imbalanced news dataset and studying the link between synthetic data quality and downstream classification performance. The authors run eight CTGAN architectures, varying noise, generator, and discriminator dimensions, as one of the two generators (alongside TabFairGAN) used for actual data augmentation experiments, while TGAN is discussed but not run. CTGAN, the SDV-family conditional tabular GAN, is thus one of the two generators actually run to produce the synthetic minority-class data underlying the paper's augmentation results.
paper-gans-panorama-synthetic-generation.needs: Not fully certain whether INESC TEC should be classed nonprofit vs other (research institute), left as nonprofit given its status as a Portuguese associate laboratory.

paper-igamt-privacy-preserving-electroni.summary: This paper proposes IGAMT, a framework for generating privacy-preserving synthetic electronic health records that handles heterogeneous temporal and non-temporal features, structurally missing values, and irregular measurement frequencies while achieving differential privacy. It is evaluated against baseline and state-of-the-art EHR synthesis models on resemblance and downstream task performance. CTGAN is mentioned only in related work as prior art built for tabular medical data that cannot be directly applied to EHR data, and is not run in the experiments.

paper-micromechanics-microstructure-mach.summary: This paper presents a machine learning approach grounded in micromechanics and microstructural analysis to predict the tensile behaviour of cement pastes, focusing on the influence of porosity and hydrated phases. It is aimed at improving predictive modelling in cement/concrete materials science. The work cites the TGAN paper, but the evidence available gives no indication of how or whether TGAN was actually used in the study.
paper-micromechanics-microstructure-mach.needs: Full text not obtained; only metadata available. Cannot confirm whether TGAN was run, adapted, or merely cited in a reference list.

paper-multi-objective-optimization-engin.summary: This paper builds a mixture-design optimization framework for engineered cementitious composite (ECC), using literature-derived datasets of tensile stress and strain, augmented data to train machine-learning surrogate models tuned via the Hunger Games Search algorithm, and an NSGA-III multi-objective optimizer to balance tensile performance against cost. Data scarcity is addressed with a 'Tuned-CTGAN', a constraints-modified Conditional Tabular GAN that enforces domain-specific mixture constraints while generating synthetic ECC mixture data, improving downstream prediction R^2. SDV's CTGAN architecture is adapted and extended with custom constraints to serve as the paper's core data-augmentation generator.
paper-multi-objective-optimization-engin.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether Tuned-CTGAN modifies the sdv-dev CTGAN implementation directly or is a from-scratch reimplementation with added constraint layers.

paper-peak-ultimate-stress-strain-2024.summary: This paper develops a hybrid machine learning framework to predict peak and ultimate axial stress-strain responses of confined ultra-high-performance concrete, combining extreme gradient boosting, gradient boosting machine, support vector regression, and K-nearest neighbors. Because available experimental data on confined UHPC specimens is scarce, the authors use an Optuna-optimized CTGAN to generate synthetic tabular data conditioned on a compiled literature database, which is then used to train and evaluate the hybrid ML model. CTGAN is run as the generator producing the synthetic augmentation data underlying the entire empirical study.
paper-peak-ultimate-stress-strain-2024.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the authors used the sdv-dev/ctgan package directly (api_user) or a custom reimplementation (port). Affiliations and venue not given in available evidence.

paper-research-knowledge-graph-gan-2024.summary: This paper proposes BAWGAN-GP, a knowledge-graph-informed WGAN-GP variant with self-attention and a BiLSTM discriminator, designed to expand imbalanced APT (advanced persistent threat) log-sequence data for intrusion detection in new power systems. The model fuses attack features extracted via random forest from a cyber threat knowledge graph into normal samples, and is validated against four baseline generation models on Precision, Recall and F1. TGAN (Xu & Veeramachaneni) is cited only in the reference list as prior work on tabular data synthesis with GANs, with no use in the paper's own methods or experiments.
paper-research-knowledge-graph-gan-2024.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN (2018) was run as one of the four baseline generators or merely cited in related work.

paper-ruleexplorer-scalable-matrix-visua.summary: This paper presents RuleExplorer, a scalable matrix-based visual analytics system for interpreting tree ensemble classifiers with tens of thousands of rules, using anomaly-biased model reduction and hierarchical visualization to preserve fidelity while supporting multi-level exploration. In a case study, a domain expert is described as having used the Synthetic Data Vault to augment test data by sampling from its distribution for evaluation purposes. SDV is only cited as the source of this expert practice and is not run, integrated, or evaluated by the authors themselves.
paper-ruleexplorer-scalable-matrix-visua.needs: The SDV mention describes a domain expert's own reported workflow during a case study, not code run by the paper's authors; treated as citation_only per the settled full-text finding.

paper-test-driven-ethics-machine-2024.summary: An opinion piece in Communications of the ACM arguing that organizations should adopt a 'test-driven ethics' approach to ML development, rooted in pragmatist discourse ethics, treating each development iteration as a testable hypothesis about ethical outcomes. The authors survey existing tools (Fairness Indicators, Aequitas, Alibi) that could support such testing. SDV is mentioned only in passing as a library that could be used to generate synthetic data to test model performance across demographic groups, without being run or engaged with further.
paper-test-driven-ethics-machine-2024.needs: Full text not obtained; only title, abstract, and a bare citation reference to the SDV paper are available, so the actual context and use (if any) of SDV cannot be determined.

paper-algorithm-drug-discovery-deep-2023.summary: This paper presents a multi-module deep-learning software platform for small-molecule anti-tumor drug discovery, applied as a case study to lung cancer, covering target identification from gene expression, inhibitor-protein interaction prediction, and IC50 forecasting for virtual pre-clinical trials. To expand a limited 514-patient gene expression dataset, the authors used the Python SDV library, specifically its CTGAN module, to generate additional synthetic patient data for the target-identification stage. SDV's CTGAN component is run directly as the generator producing augmented training data feeding into the deep learning target-selection pipeline.

paper-autonlp-framework-automated-model-.summary: This paper proposes AutoNLP, a framework for automated selection of pre-trained NLP models to reduce the computational cost of searching the model space. To build a larger meta-dataset from only forty-four text classification datasets, the authors used Copula GAN, a deep generative model, to augment the meta-dataset used for training their model-selection algorithm. SDV's CopulaGAN synthesizer is run as the tool generating this augmented meta-dataset.
paper-autonlp-framework-automated-model-.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentence available, so exact role and depth of CopulaGAN use (e.g., which SDV parameters or metadata schema) cannot be confirmed.

paper-caleb-conditional-adversarial-lear.summary: CALEB is a conditional adversarial learning framework proposed to improve social-media bot detection, likely by generating synthetic bot-like data to counter class imbalance in training sets. No abstract or full text was available to confirm the mechanism in detail. The paper cites the original 2016 SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) paper, apparently only as a reference to prior synthetic-data-generation work.
paper-caleb-conditional-adversarial-lear.needs: Full text and citing sentence were not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV is merely cited or actually used to generate synthetic bot data for CALEB's training.

paper-augmentation-guided-breast-cancer-.summary: This paper proposes an integrated deep-learning framework for breast cancer diagnosis and prognosis that first generates synthetic tabular tumor data with deep generative models and then classifies it using the interpretable TabNet architecture. It compares CTGAN and TVAE as synthetic data generators, finding TVAE produces higher-quality synthetic breast tumor data (measured via Chi-Squared and Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests), and the downstream classifier is trained solely on this synthetic output. SDV's CTGAN and TVAE synthesizers are run directly as the generators underpinning the entire data augmentation and classification pipeline.
paper-augmentation-guided-breast-cancer-.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev package was invoked directly (api_user) versus a custom reimplementation, though the abstract's phrasing strongly suggests direct use of the standard CTGAN/TVAE models.

paper-evaluating-curriculum-learning-str.summary: This paper applies Curriculum Learning to train a machine learning model for pancreatic cancer prediction using a urinary biomarker dataset, addressing missing values via imputation and class scarcity via data augmentation. The authors compare pacing functions and find exponential increasing-difficulty pacing yields the best results, with SMOTE generally outperforming CTGAN-based augmentation. CTGAN is run as one of two data augmentation methods (alongside SMOTE) to generate synthetic tabular examples, serving as an evaluated alternative rather than the paper's main contribution.
paper-evaluating-curriculum-learning-str.needs: Not explicit whether the sdv-dev CTGAN package was used or an independent implementation; treated as api_user given no reimplementation details given.

paper-federated-learning-base-station-20.summary: This paper investigates federated learning for time-series forecasting of 5G base station traffic, comparing five neural network architectures trained under a federated setting on non-identically distributed LTE data against centralized training, and also examines a large-scale synthetic-data scenario for computational/communication cost analysis. The work shows federated approaches can match centralized prediction accuracy while reducing energy and communication costs. SDV's DeepEcho sequential-model paper (PAR) is cited only in the reference list, with no engagement in the body text.
paper-federated-learning-base-station-20.needs: Bibliographic-only citation; no indication of actual use of DeepEcho/PAR in the study.

paper-qast-rare-relational-2023.summary: Proposes QAST, which synthesizes rare-class relational records and then judges its own output, attaching semantic pseudo-labels to generated samples and filtering them by a learned quality estimate so that self-training does not amplify bad synthetic data, addressing the fact that GAN samples arrive without reliable labels. CTGAN is both a compared baseline in the distribution figures and the design QAST's own generator follows: the shared GAN module's generator and the normalization of the original samples are taken from Xu et al.

paper-redactor-centric-individualized-de.summary: Redactor is a data-centric defense against inference attacks that generates 'disinformation' examples to insert into unlabeled training data, diluting a target individual's information without needing access to the victim model or its training process. The authors approximate an unknown labeler via a probabilistic decision boundary combining surrogate classifiers, then generate realistic disinformation points near this boundary. To produce these realistic tabular examples, they extend CTGAN's architecture, adapting its mode-specific normalization and conditional generation mechanism into their own generator, and compare against a 'GAN only' ablation using CTGAN alone.
paper-redactor-centric-individualized-de.needs: The evidence header lists the cited SDV paper as the 2018 TGAN work, but the body text clearly extends CTGAN (Xu et al. 2019); component/concept fields follow the body text's actual target.

paper-synthetic-evaluation-metrics-machi.summary: This book chapter is a literature review surveying synthetic data generation methods (CART, Synthpop, SDV, PrivBayes, GANs) and the utility, privacy, and fairness metrics used to validate them. It does not propose a new generator or run experiments itself, instead summarizing prior studies' approaches and findings on synthetic data quality. SDV is described in prose, citing Patki et al.'s work using a copula-based statistical model to build a generative model of relational databases for producing synthetic structured data.
paper-synthetic-evaluation-metrics-machi.needs: The paper also discusses other works (e.g., Hittmeir et al.) that used SDV, but this chapter itself only cites/describes it in a review context, not running it.

paper-differentially-private-normalizing.summary: The paper proposes DP-HFlow, a differentially private normalizing flow model for synthesizing heterogeneous tabular data, introducing a conditional spline flow to reduce parameter complexity and fine-grained gradient clipping strategies for private training. It is evaluated against DP-CGAN, GS-WGAN, and DP-MERF under differential privacy, and against CTGAN in the non-private setting on datasets like Adult, Census, Covertype, and Intrusion. CTGAN is run unmodified as a non-private baseline generator, with its ML-efficacy results reported alongside the authors' own model.

paper-fingan-chaotic-generative-adversar.summary: This paper proposes ChaoticGAN, a GAN variant using chaotic noise as generator input to oversample minority classes in three severely imbalanced banking/insurance datasets (churn, insurance fraud, loan default), and combines it with one-class SVM undersampling before training several ML classifiers. The proposed ChaoticGAN and its hybrid are compared statistically against traditional GAN, WGAN, and CTGAN as baselines across all three datasets. CTGAN is run unmodified as one of several baseline data generators, and its output feeds classifiers whose AUC is benchmarked against the authors' proposed method.
paper-fingan-chaotic-generative-adversar.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether the sdv-dev package or an independent CTGAN reimplementation was used, though 'no changes to its architecture' suggests the original model was run as-is.

paper-comment-gmd-2020-427-2-2021.summary: This is a peer-review comment (or associated discussion item) on a manuscript exploring copula-based statistical models to generate synthetically augmented training data for a neural-network emulator of downwelling longwave radiation, reporting up to 62% reduction in mean absolute error over the non-augmented baseline. The underlying work concerns copula-based synthetic data generation for weather/climate ML emulation but the evidence available gives no citing sentence, only that the original SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) systems paper is listed among its references. SDV's founding paper is cited as prior related work on copula-based synthetic data generation, with no indication the SDV software itself was run.
paper-comment-gmd-2020-427-2-2021.needs: No full text or citing sentence was available; this document type is a peer-review comment on a GMD discussion paper and it is unclear whether SDV is discussed as related work or only listed in references. Cannot confirm whether a specific SDV concept (e.g., Gaussian copula) is invoked.

paper-synthesis-differentially-private-m.summary: This paper proposes PrivMRF, a differentially-private data synthesis method that selects low-dimensional noisy marginals to build a Markov random field capturing attribute correlations, then uses this MRF to generate synthetic high-dimensional data. Experiments on four benchmark datasets show it outperforms prior DP synthesis methods on counting queries and downstream classification accuracy. The paper cites the original SDV paper as related work on synthetic data generation, without any indication it runs or extends SDV's software.
paper-synthesis-differentially-private-m.needs: Full text and the actual citing sentence were not obtained; cannot confirm how or whether SDV is discussed beyond being listed as a cited work.

paper-data-sharing-economy-2021.summary: Gives data providers attribute-wise knobs to trade privacy against the value a recipient can extract, using two regularizers on a GAN objective rather than obfuscating attributes outright. CTGAN is cited among the generative approaches that preserve statistical properties; the work extends WGAN-GP instead.

paper-synthetic-ageing-occupant-behaviou.summary: A pilot study from NTU's ageing research institute that synthesizes household occupant-behaviour profiles for older adults so that building-energy simulation can proceed without collecting or distributing real survey data, which the authors describe as expensive and constrained by privacy. Survey responses from 600 Singapore participants in two cohorts (40-64 and 65 and above), recruited through senior activity centres, record demographics and daily usage times for air conditioning, fan, lighting, kettle, electric iron, washing machine, refrigerator, TV, computer and rice cooker, joined to average monthly household electricity consumption by postal code. The pipeline has three steps: generate 600 synthetic records, reduce them by three-dimensional homogeneity analysis and k-means into three personas, and simulate a year of each persona's occupancy schedule in EnergyPlus 8.9.0 against HDB building constructions. Kullback-Leibler divergence between the real and synthetic personas stays within 0.46, simulated and real annual electricity consumption differ by 0.8, 2.5 and 8.1 percent across the three personas, and the resulting energy use intensity of 48.21 kWh per square metre per year falls inside the residential range reported elsewhere, which the authors take as evidence the profiles are realistic enough for design use. CTGAN is the only generator, chosen over a plain GAN because random sampling during training under-represents minority categorical columns, and it is run from its published Python package. The entry therefore records CTGAN as the sole synthesizer of the study's data, cited to Xu et al. and linked to its PyPI distribution.

paper-ensemblentldetect-intelligent-fram.summary: This paper proposes EnsembleNTLDetect, a framework for detecting electricity theft in smart grid data that combines eDTWBI-based imputation, near-miss undersampling, stacked autoencoders for dimensionality reduction, and a soft voting ensemble classifier, validated on real-world SGCC consumption data. CTGAN is used to augment the training data after undersampling, generating thousands of synthetic samples to balance the genuine and theft classes and improve classifier robustness. CTGAN's mode-specific normalization is explicitly adopted for the numerical consumption data, while its generator is run directly as the data augmentation stage of the pipeline.

paper-implicit-generative-copulas-2021.summary: Proposes Implicit Generative Copula (IGC) models, which learn a multivariate latent distribution via an implicit generative neural network and enforce marginal uniformity through the probability integral transform, avoiding the parametric or tree-structure restrictions of classical and vine copulas. The method is evaluated against Gaussian and vine copulas, GMMNs, and a VAE on synthetic, financial, and image data. SDV is cited only in passing in the introduction as an example of synthetic tabular data generation being a popular application of copulas.

paper-machine-learning-predictions-covid.summary: This paper uses a Susceptible-Infected-Removed (SIR) model coupled with a Random Forest machine learning algorithm to predict the end-time of the second COVID-19 wave in Indian states, calibrating the model on first-wave data and simulating synthetic training data from the SIR model itself. It also studies how testing rate and lattice site-dilution (percolation) affect the predictability of the model. The SDV paper is cited only in passing as a general reference for the well-known technique of using synthetic data to enhance ML prediction capability, with no SDV software used to generate any of the paper's synthetic data.

paper-graph-convolutional-network-genera.summary: This conference paper addresses the algorithm selection problem for classification by proposing a GCN-based GAN that generates synthetic classification datasets represented as weighted graphs, extending prior work (LM-GAN) rather than tabular matrix convolutions. It contributes a graph-based discriminator that jointly predicts dataset realism and algorithm performance for meta-learning purposes. CTGAN is cited only briefly in the introduction as a prior GAN-based dataset synthesis method, without being run or adopted in the proposed method.
paper-graph-convolutional-network-genera.needs: Full text not obtained; only abstract and citing sentence available, so cannot verify any deeper engagement with CTGAN beyond this passing mention.

paper-synsiggan-generative-adversarial-n.summary: This paper proposes SynSigGAN, a GAN using a bidirectional grid LSTM generator and CNN discriminator to synthesize biomedical time-series signals (ECG, EEG, EMG, PPG) for healthcare research and education while preserving patient confidentiality. It compares performance against traditional and other GAN models using correlation-based evaluation metrics. The SDV paper is only cited in a general remark about researchers finding no significant statistical difference between original and synthetic data, with no SDV code or method used in the work.

paper-wild-blueberry-yield-prediction-20.summary: This paper develops a hybrid pipeline combining a process-based computer simulation model with machine learning algorithms to predict wild blueberry crop yield. It is an agricultural modeling study unrelated to synthetic tabular data generation in its core methodology. SDV is cited only in passing, in the introduction, as an example of a general-purpose simulated data generator for data science experiments.
paper-wild-blueberry-yield-prediction-20.needs: Only one citing sentence available; full text and abstract not obtained, so cannot confirm whether SDV is discussed further in the body.

paper-enhancing-discrete-event-simulatio.summary: A literature review examining how discrete-event simulation (DES) intersects with big data analytics approaches such as data mining, machine learning, data farming, visual analytics, and process mining, proposing a framework for a DES development methodology that incorporates these analytics techniques. The review surveys use-cases across application domains rather than running any experiments itself. SDV is only cited in passing, as the source for the term 'synthetic data' used to describe data generated from models.

preprint-causal-privacy-audit-workflow-2.summary: This paper introduces CaP-Eval, a decision-facing causal-privacy audit workflow that compares original, distilled, adversarial-synthetic, statistical-synthetic (Gaussian Copula), and differentially-private (DPGNet) student data on predictive utility, treatment-effect fidelity, estimator robustness, and privacy-governance risk, using a university dropout dataset with financial-status covariates. It finds that DPGNet and distilled data preserve causal treatment-effect structure more reliably than the SDV-based adversarial and Gaussian Copula baselines, which attenuate effect magnitudes. SDV's CTGAN-based synthesizer and its GaussianCopula synthesizer are both run through SDV's metadata workflow as two of the several generated-data baselines evaluated in the audit.
preprint-causal-privacy-audit-workflow-2.needs: University of Cambridge appears in the affiliation block but is not linked to any author via the superscript numbering given; excluded from author affiliations as unverifiable.

paper-synthony-selection-agent-2026.summary: Treats the choice of tabular synthesizer as the problem worth automating rather than the supply of synthesizers, profiling a dataset along four interpretable stress dimensions - long-tailed marginals, high-cardinality categoricals, Zipfian imbalance and small-sample size - and matching that profile against a capability registry to pick a generator that minimizes regret against an intent-specific oracle, given a user preference over fidelity, privacy and utility. SDV is both prior art and pool: it is named twice as the open-source library that democratized access to individual synthesizers and provides unified APIs and benchmarking but leaves model selection to the user, which is the gap the selection layer fills, it is credited for Gaussian Copulas in the statistical lineage, and TVAE is one of the ten candidate synthesizers the framework selects among.

preprint-synthetic-rna-seq-cohorts-2026.summary: This preprint proposes a multi-axis benchmark for synthetic bulk RNA-seq cohort generation, evaluating three generative approaches (dbTwin, class-MVN, and PCA-CTGAN) across oncology, sepsis, and pediatric IBD datasets on biological fidelity, downstream ML utility (TSTR/SHAP concordance), and memorization-based privacy risk. The goal is to establish practical guidance for privacy-preserving sharing of transcriptomic data. One of the three benchmarked generators, PCA-CTGAN, is described as an extension of CTGAN that runs the model in PCA-compressed feature space, making CTGAN one of several generators evaluated in the study.
preprint-synthetic-rna-seq-cohorts-2026.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether PCA-CTGAN modifies CTGAN's internal architecture (derivative_work) or simply applies unmodified CTGAN to PCA-transformed features (api_user/composition) — judged as the latter based on the abstract's phrasing.

paper-tcsdg-agriculture-2026.summary: Reframes tabular synthesis for scarce agricultural reference data as a supervised problem rather than an unconditional mimicking one: a teacher model scores candidate rows for plausibility, informativeness and non-redundancy, and only samples that preserve the feature-target relationship survive, which is what separates useful augmentation from statistically realistic but task-misaligned samples. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the six established generators run for comparison, taken from the Synthcity library, and both are reported as failing to deliver positive utility on crop-type classification or yield prediction.

preprint-neuro-symbolic-classification-b.summary: This paper presents a neuro-symbolic method that compiles Description Logic ontologies into probabilistic circuits, enabling tractable deductive reasoning, synthetic dataset generation reflecting ontology semantics, and neural classifiers whose predictions are consistent with the ontology. It demonstrates faster reasoning than existing DL reasoners and competitive or superior classification performance versus neural baselines while guaranteeing logical consistency. The SDV paper is cited only in passing, as one of several references supporting the general claim that training and testing models on synthetic data is a widespread ML technique.

preprint-diagnostic-support-system-inter.summary: This preprint develops an interpretable machine-learning diagnostic pipeline that uses respiratory oscillometry parameters to detect respiratory dysfunction in silicosis patients, comparing classifiers such as EBM, CatBoost, Random Forest and the HyperTab deep-learning model on a small clinical dataset (109 volunteers). To counter the small sample size, the authors augment the training data using two synthetic data generation approaches, labeled FAST_ML and CTGAN, boosting the training set to 150 samples before re-running the classifiers. CTGAN, part of the SDV family, is run directly as one of the synthetic-data generators used to augment the training data, with the paper reporting CTGAN-augmented results as its best-performing scenario.
preprint-diagnostic-support-system-inter.needs: Assumes 'FAST_ML' and 'CTGAN' scenario labels correspond to SDV's preset synthesizer modes rather than a separate custom pipeline; no explicit sdv package import or version cited in the visible text.

preprint-democratizing-tabular-access-op.summary: This paper presents the MOSTLY AI Synthetic Data SDK, an open-source Python toolkit built on the TabularARGN autoregressive framework that supports single-table, multi-table and sequential tabular data synthesis with built-in differential privacy, fairness-aware generation, and automated quality assurance. The authors benchmark their SDK's flat-table synthesis against CTGAN and several other generators, and separately compare its multi-table/relational handling against the Synthetic Data Vault (SDV), reporting that SDV struggled on a two-table dataset with complex relational and temporal dependencies where their SDK performed better. Both CTGAN and SDV are run as evaluation baselines rather than adopted or modified, with SDV's relational synthesis capability being the specific target of the comparative experiments.

paper-hctgan-multi-tabular-2024.summary: Proposes HCTGAN for relational databases, with a training algorithm that passes information from parent-table generators into the noise vector of child-table generators and a sampling algorithm that walks the schema so referential integrity holds by construction, and reports that it samples large volumes far faster than the probabilistic alternative at slightly lower quality. HCTGAN is presented as an extended version of CTGAN, keeping its generator loss and training-by-sampling and adding the parent conditioning on top; the comparison is against SDV's HMA1, on datasets shipped with the SDV Python library and scored with SDMetrics.

preprint-kipps-knowledge-infusion-privac.summary: KIPPS is a synthetic tabular data generation framework that infuses domain and regulatory knowledge from knowledge graphs into generative deep learning models, aiming to enforce domain constraints and improve realism while preserving privacy, evaluated on cybersecurity and healthcare datasets against differentially-private baselines. The authors adopt CTGAN's mode-specific normalization scheme in their own model's representation of continuous attributes, and separately run TVAE as one of several state-of-the-art baseline generators (alongside DPCTGAN, DPWGAN, PATEGAN) reporting its statistical-utility and privacy-attack results in comparison tables. TVAE (from the CTGAN paper) is thus used both as an adopted normalization technique and as a benchmarked generator against which KIPPS is compared.
preprint-kipps-knowledge-infusion-privac.needs: Whether TVAE was run via the sdv-dev/CTGAN package directly or reimplemented is not stated explicitly, though numeric results are reported as if executed.

preprint-elusive-pursuit-reproducing-pat.summary: This paper reproduces, benchmarks, and audits six open-source implementations of PATE-GAN, a differentially private GAN for tabular data, finding that none replicate the original utility results and that all leak more privacy than intended, uncovering 19 privacy violations and 5 other bugs. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing, cited as a non-DP model that a prior study found less private than one PATE-GAN implementation under a membership-inference attack, with no experiment run on it in this paper.

paper-curated-llm-lowdata-2023.summary: Argues that in the low-data regime a generator fitted to a handful of rows cannot invent structure it never saw, and proposes drawing candidate rows from a large language model's prior instead, then discarding the ones a learning-dynamics curation step marks as hard or ambiguous, so only samples the downstream model can actually use survive. CTGAN and TVAE are the conventional tabular generators the argument is set against and the comparison is run against: TVAE is the head-to-head generator in the extrapolation study and in the per-subgroup accuracy gains, where it loses ground on the smallest groups while the language model gains.

paper-fs-tgan-iot-ids-2023.summary: Proposes an IoT intrusion detection approach pairing feature selection with a tabular GAN. The name Fs-TGAN indicates a TGAN variant, but no abstract is indexed, so whether the generator is modified or merely applied is unestablished.

preprint-method-generating-synthetic-com.summary: This preprint proposes a dual-generative-model pipeline that combines an auto-encoding GAN (αGAN) for chest X-ray image dimensionality reduction with a tabular GAN to jointly synthesize hybrid medical records containing both chest radiographs and non-image clinical variables, evaluated via downstream classification/regression tasks on real vs. synthetic training data. The tabular generation stage is performed by CTGAN, explicitly run as the standalone open-source library (version 0.7.4) to model the encoded image features plus clinical variables and produce the synthetic dataset that anchors the entire empirical evaluation.

paper-mox2-sensor-semantic-2023.summary: Represents physical activity sensor observations semantically and compares real against synthetic versions of the same stream, working from wearable data collected at scale. Gaussian Copula, CTGAN and TabGAN generate the synthetic datasets, so two SDV synthesizers sit alongside an outside generator in the comparison.

paper-syndiffix-accurate-synthetic-data-.summary: Presents SynDiffix, an anonymising structured-data synthesizer built on the Diffix line of work, and argues that being able to run a query over synthetic data is not the same as getting an accurate answer, reporting over twice the median accuracy of the alternatives. SDV appears as one of five compared products: CTGAN 0.18.0 is taken from sdv.dev and is the named point of comparison in the abstract, so the library is run purely as the baseline the new tool is measured against.

paper-fct-gan-fourier-2022.summary: Argues that tabular GANs miss correlations spanning the whole row and are sensitive to the order in which columns are presented, and proposes FCT-GAN, which tokenizes each encoded row with a CNN filter and then passes the tokens through Fourier network blocks in both generator and discriminator so that learnable weights over all frequencies capture global column relations. The paper first demonstrates the permutation problem empirically across three column orders, then reports the smallest variation for its own model. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five synthesizers it benchmarks throughout, and the conditional vector FCT-GAN adopts is the one the paper attributes to CTGAN and describes as later improved by CTAB-GAN+, together with the variational Gaussian mixture encoding of continuous columns.

paper-fingan-crm-banking-2022.summary: Attacks class imbalance in banking and insurance analytics two ways: oversampling the minority class with a GAN, and a hybrid that first reduces the majority class to the support vectors found by a one-class SVM before oversampling, tested on churn prediction, auto insurance fraud and loan default with six classifiers and a statistical significance test. CTGAN is one of the three generators run unmodified as the oversampler, and the paper's conclusion rests on it: it forms a headline column of the results tables for all three datasets and the CTGAN-based approaches are the ones reported as best.

paper-cystic-fibrosis-ehr-2022.summary: Synthesises cystic fibrosis electronic health records from the IBM Explorys dataset to address class imbalance in mortality-risk prediction, and evaluates four generators on authenticity, fidelity and diversity before using their samples to augment the minority class, finding that augmentation improves two of four downstream models while trading against similarity to the real records. CTGAN is one of the four compared generators, implemented from the architecture and code repository of Xu et al. (2019), and its behaviour on duplication, precision, density and coverage is reported alongside the variational autoencoder and the two differentially private GANs.

preprint-estimation-local-time-varying-2.summary: This preprint studies how misclassification errors between local and imported disease cases bias estimates of the local time-varying reproduction number, and proposes a Bayesian framework to correct for such identification errors, illustrated with simulations and COVID-19 outbreak data from Hong Kong and Victoria, Australia. The SDV paper appears only in the reference list, with no SDV-family term found anywhere in the body text.

preprint-pedagogical-rule-extraction-lea.summary: This preprint introduces PRELIM, a framework that unifies existing pedagogical rule-extraction (PRE) methods, which augment small datasets using a 'generator' model plus a black-box labeler before training an interpretable white-box rule-based model (decision trees, classification rules, subgroup discovery). The authors run extensive experiments across many datasets to identify which generator/white-box combinations actually improve accuracy under interpretability constraints. The paper's metadata records a citation to the TGAN (2018) paper, but no passage in the extracted full text names TGAN, CTGAN, or any SDV-family term, so the citation could not be located in context.

preprint-synthesising-multi-modal-minori.summary: This paper proposes a latent-space interpolation framework for oversampling the minority class in imbalanced tabular classification: an autoencoder maps mixed continuous/discrete samples into a dense latent space, interpolation is performed there, and synthetic points are decoded back to the original feature space. The method is evaluated against numerous oversamplers (SMOTE variants, Poly, VAE/AAE/ACAI-based methods, GAN-based methods) across 27 real-world datasets using cover/error and downstream ROC-AUC metrics. CTGAN, run via its open-source implementation (github.com/sdv-dev/CTGAN), and TGAN are included as two of many baseline oversamplers, and both are ultimately found to underperform the proposed autoencoder-based approach.

The paper is on explainable ML visualization tooling, not tabular data synthesis. preprint-improving-lime-robustness-smart.summary: This workshop paper proposes CTGAN-LIME, a method that replaces LIME's naive Gaussian perturbation sampler with a conditional GAN trained to generate more realistic local synthetic data, improving robustness against adversarial attacks like Fooling-LIME while preserving explanation quality. The authors implement the CTGAN architecture themselves, describing its WGAN loss, conditional vector, and discriminator-based filtering of unrealistic samples used during LIME's sampling and inference. CTGAN's conditional tabular GAN design (mode-specific normalization for multi-modal/non-Gaussian variables and its conditional vector) is reimplemented from scratch as the paper's entire generative core, not imported from the SDV library.

preprint-sequence-preserving-network-tra.summary: This paper presents the Network Traffic Generator (NTG), a framework that perturbs recorded enterprise network traffic to produce diverse but realistic background traffic for network simulation and what-if analysis, profiling flows with 200 cross-protocol features and modeling sequences of network activities via Markov and neural language models. The SDV paper appears only in the reference list among general citations motivating the usefulness of synthetic data, with no SDV code, model, or concept engaged in the method.

preprint-tool-framework-tweaking-feature.summary: This paper introduces ASPECT, a framework for scaling empirical datasets to a desired size while preserving user-selected features, aimed at application-specific database benchmarking. It shifts from the traditional feature-extraction-then-synthesis pipeline to a scale-then-tweak approach, using independent tweaking tools to enforce desired properties on the scaled dataset. The Synthetic Data Vault is cited only as one of several prior works following the older feature-extraction-based synthetic data generation framework that ASPECT departs from.

repo-nlp-master-2025.summary: Syllabus and notebooks for a master's-level natural language processing course running from text preprocessing to large language models. Its data-generation unit teaches SDV directly: `synthetic_data_generation.ipynb` loads a demo table with `sdv.datasets.demo.download_demo`, describes it with `SingleTableMetadata` and fits a `CTGANSynthesizer`. SDV's demo loader and conditional GAN are run as the teaching example for synthetic data.

repo-dive2gai.summary: A Russian-language self-education programme working through generative AI from the earliest generative models to current ones, one unit per topic at two levels of depth. Unit 9 is tabular GANs, taught on SDV: the notebook imports `CTGAN` and `TVAE` from `ctgan` and unpacks the mixed-type encoding with RDT's `ClusterBasedNormalizer`. SDV's two neural synthesizers are run as the worked example for the tabular unit.

repo-dss-workshop.summary: Workshop material on synthetic data, shipped as an exercise notebook and a worked solution. It is an SDV course from end to end: the solution builds a `SingleTableMetadata`, explains and fits `GaussianCopulaSynthesizer`, `CTGANSynthesizer` and `TVAESynthesizer` in turn with prose describing what each model is, reports `evaluate_quality` and SDMetrics' `NewRowSynthesis`, and closes on RDT's `AnonymizedFaker` for the PII columns. SDV's three synthesizers, its evaluation and RDT's anonymising transformer are the workshop's whole syllabus.
